### Financial Institutions, Inc. Reports Net Income Available to Common Shareholders of $19.6 million, or $0.99 per Diluted Share, for the Third Quarter of 2026


October 29, 2026


Quarterly results highlighted by loan growth of 2.2% and deposit growth of 3.3%


WARSAW, N.Y., Oct. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Financial Institutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: FISI) (the "Company," "we" or "us") today reported financial and operational results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, reflecting strong performance by subsidiaries Five Star Bank (the "Bank") and Courier Capital, LLC ("Courier Capital"), including healthy loan and deposit growth and sustained profitability.

**Third Quarter 2026 Highlights and Key Developments**


- Total loans grew 2.2% from the end of the linked quarter and 5.8% from September 30, 2025, to reach $4.86 billion at September 30, 2026, driven by robust commercial lending.
- Total deposits increased 3.3% quarter-over-quarter and 2.2% year-over-year to $5.47 billion at September 30, 2026. Growth was broad-based across all deposit categories, led by seasonal support in public deposits.
- Net interest income reached a new quarterly high of $54.3 million and net interest margin of 3.70% was stable with the linked quarter and up 5 basis points from the year-ago quarter.
- Investment advisory income, the Company's leading contributor of noninterest income, increased 1.7% and 10.6% from the linked and year-ago quarters, respectively.
- The efficiency ratio remained below 57% for the quarter, reflecting the Company's focus on sustained profitability.
- The Company's strong capital position enabled the repurchase of 185,833 shares of common stock at an average price of $40.92 per share during the quarter.


"Our third quarter results underscore the strength of our relationship-driven business model and our unwavering commitment to disciplined execution," said President and Chief Executive Officer Martin K. Birmingham. "Our commercial franchise continues to be the primary driver of loan growth and was supported by increases in consumer indirect and residential mortgage lending during the third quarter. While our quarterly net charge-off ratio was up from lower-than-typical levels in the linked and year-ago quarters, it remains within our full-year guidance. At the same time, the ratio of non-performing loans to total loans decreased by 3 basis points. Overall, we remain focused on credit-disciplined loan production in our core Upstate New York markets."


Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer W. Jack Plants II added, "Third quarter performance benefited from continued growth in average earning assets and effective balance sheet management, supporting a 3.70% net interest margin and a nearly 5% increase in net interest income from the prior year period. Our balance sheet remains a source of strength, reflected in a tangible common equity ratio(1) of 8.40%, a common equity Tier 1 ratio of 11.36%, and a return on average tangible common equity(1) of 13.75%. These strong capital levels provide us flexibility to support loan growth and thoughtful investments in our business, while continuing to return capital to shareholders through share buybacks, as we did during the third quarter with the repurchase of 185,833 shares."

Net interest income was $54.3 million, up $930 thousand from the linked quarter and up $2.5 million from the third quarter of 2025. Net interest margin of 3.70% was consistent with the linked quarter and up 5 basis points from the year-ago quarter, driven by lower interest-bearing liability costs.


- Average interest-earning assets of $5.84 billion were up $51.6 million from the second quarter of 2026 and up $180.7 million from the third quarter of 2025. The linked quarter variance reflected a $114.5 million increase in average loans, partially offset by decreases in the average balances of investment securities of $61.6 million and Federal Reserve interest-earning cash of $1.2 million. The year-over-year variance reflected a $228.2 million increase in the average balance of loans, partially offset by a $43.2 million decrease in the average balance of investment securities and a $4.3 million decrease in the average balance of Federal Reserve interest-earning cash. The average yield on interest-earning assets was 5.79% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 5.76% in the second quarter of 2026, and 5.93% in the third quarter of 2025.
- Average interest-bearing liabilities of $4.57 billion were up $13.8 million from the second quarter of 2026 and up $135.5 million from the third quarter of 2025. The linked quarter variance was primarily due to increases in the average balances of time, savings and money market deposits, partially offset by decreases in average interest-bearing demand deposits and short-term borrowings, while average long-term borrowings were flat. The year-over-year variance reflected increases in the average balances of savings and money market deposits, time deposits, short-term borrowings and interest-bearing demand deposits, partially offset by a decrease in average long-term borrowings. The average cost of interest-bearing liabilities was 2.67%, reflecting an increase of 6 basis points from the linked quarter and a decrease of 25 basis points from the year-ago quarter.

Noninterest income was $10.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, versus $11.0 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $12.1 million in the third quarter of 2025. The linked quarter variance was primarily driven by decreased income from derivative instruments, net, or swap fees, along with greater losses on investments in limited partnerships. The aforementioned lower level of swap fees and loss on limited partnerships were also contributors to the year-over-year variance. Detail on other select categories with notable variances follows:


- Investment advisory income of $3.3 million was up from both the linked and year-ago quarters, reflecting both new business and market performance.
- A loss on investments in limited partnerships, which are primarily small business investment companies, of $274 thousand was recognized in the third quarter of 2026, compared to a loss of $140 thousand and a gain of $223 thousand in the linked and year-ago quarters, respectively. Income from these investments, which we account for under the equity method, fluctuates based on the maturity and performance of the underlying investments.
- Income from derivative instruments, net, which is based on the number and value of interest rate swap transactions executed during the quarter, of $106 thousand was down from $518 thousand and $847 thousand in the linked and year-ago quarters, respectively.
- A net gain on investment securities of $703 thousand was recorded in the third quarter of 2025. There was no gain or loss recorded in the second or third quarters of 2026.
- Other noninterest income of $1.2 million was relatively flat with the linked quarter and down from the year-ago quarter, driven by a variety of factors.

Noninterest expense was $36.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $35.6 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $35.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. Detail on select categories with notable variances follows:


- Salaries and employee benefits expense was $489 thousand higher than the second quarter of 2026, primarily driven by an increase in health insurance benefit expense, and $1.1 million higher than the third quarter of 2025, reflecting a combination of factors, including annual merit increases, higher incentive compensation and investments in personnel.

Total loans of $4.86 billion at September 30, 2026 were up $102.9 million from the end of the linked quarter and up $265.4 million from September 30, 2025.


- Strong commercial lending activity in the Bank's Western and Central New York markets drove both the linked quarter and year-over-year growth.


Total deposits were $5.47 billion at September 30, 2026, up $175.5 million from June 30, 2026, and up $117.1 million from September 30, 2025.


- The linked quarter variance was primarily due to seasonally higher public deposit balances, but reflected growth across all deposit types. The year-over-year increase reflected higher nonpublic, reciprocal and brokered deposits, partially offset by a modest decrease in public deposits. Public deposits represented 22% of total deposits at September 30, 2026, 22% at June 30, 2026, and 23% at September 30, 2025.

Shareholders' equity was $619.0 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $643.4 million at June 30, 2026, and $621.7 million at September 30, 2025. The decline was primarily the result of an increase in accumulated other comprehensive loss associated with unrealized losses in the available for sale securities portfolio, which was driven by the increase in interest rates, as well as stock repurchases during the third quarter of 2026, partially offset by net income, net of dividends, retained.


The Company declared a common stock dividend of $0.32 per common share in the third quarter of 2026, consistent with the linked quarter and reflecting an increase of $0.01, or 3.2%, over the year-ago quarter, returning 32% of third quarter net income to common shareholders.


During the third quarter of 2026, the Company repurchased 185,833 shares of common stock at an average price of $40.92 per share. As of September 30, 2026, 320,480 shares remained available under the repurchase program that was approved in September 2025 and which does not have an expiration date.

The Company has remained strategically focused on the importance of credit discipline, allocating resources to credit and risk management functions as the loan portfolio has grown.


- Non-performing loans were $38.5 million, or 0.79% of total loans, at September 30, 2026, a modest decrease from the linked quarter. The increase from one year prior primarily reflects one well-collateralized commercial business loan that moved to nonaccrual status in the first quarter of 2026, offset in part by the partial charge-off of a previously disclosed nonaccrual commercial business relationship for which a specific reserve was in place.
- Provision for credit losses was $3.9 million in the third quarter of 2026 and was driven by a combination of factors, including loan growth and fluctuation in the balance of unfunded commitments. The provision for credit losses on unfunded commitments, which is included in the provision for credit losses as required by the current expected credit loss standard, totaled a credit of $663 thousand in the third quarter of 2026, compared to a credit of $1.0 million in the second quarter of 2026 and a provision of $671 thousand in the third quarter of 2025.

**About Financial Institutions, Inc.**


Financial Institutions, Inc. (NASDAQ: FISI) is a financial holding company with approximately $6.5 billion in assets offering banking and wealth management products and services. Its Five Star Bank subsidiary provides consumer and commercial banking and lending services to individuals, municipalities and businesses through banking locations spanning Western and Central New York and a commercial loan production office serving the Mid-Atlantic region. Its Courier Capital, LLC subsidiary offers customized investment management, consulting and retirement plan services to individuals, businesses, institutions, foundations and retirement plans. Learn more at FISI-Investors.com.
